arxiv-2412-12293.title: Stable Andrews–Curtis conjecture via fake surfaces and Zeeman conjecture
arxiv-2412-12293.creator: Lucas Fagan, Yang Qiu, Zhenghan Wang
arxiv-2412-12293.description: Abstract . We propose an induction scheme that aims at establishing the stable Andrews–Curtis conjecture in the affirmative. The stable Andrews–Curtis conjecture is equivalent to the conjecture that every contractible fake surface is 3-deformable to a point. We prove that every contractible fake surface of complexity less than 6 is 3-deformable to a point by induction. 1.

arxiv-2504-09730.title: Learning-based decentralized control with collision avoidance for multi-agent systems*
arxiv-2504-09730.creator: Omayra Yago Nieto, Alexandre Anahory Simoes, Juan I. Giribet, Leonardo J. Colombo
arxiv-2504-09730.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a learning-based tracking controller based on Gaussian processes (GP) for collision avoidance of multi-agent systems where the agents evolve in the special Euclidean group in the space SE(3). In particular, we use GPs to estimate certain uncertainties that appear in the dynamics of the agents.

arxiv-2509-11015.title: California Wildfire Inventory (CAWFI): An Extensive Dataset for Predictive Techniques based on Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2509-11015.creator: Rohan Tan Bhowmik, Youn Soo Jung, Juan Aguilera, Mary Prunicki, Kari Nadeau
arxiv-2509-11015.description: Abstract Due to climate change and the disruption of ecosystems worldwide, wildfires are increasingly impacting environment, infrastructure, and human lives globally. Additionally, an exacerbating climate crisis means that these losses would continue to grow if preventative measures are not implemented. Though recent advancements in artificial intelligence enable wildfire management techniques, most deployed solutions focus on detecting wildfires after ignition.

Recent surveys have revealed that planets residing in the desert are dense ( ρ ≳ 1 {\rho}{\gtrsim}1 g/cm 3 ), massive ( ∼ \sim 10 − {-} 50 M ⊕ M_{\oplus} ), and orbit metal-rich stars that are indistinguishable from those hosting hot Jupiters. However, their origins remain mysterious.

pmc-10713827.creator: Andrea Di Credico, Amélie Weiss, Massimo Corsini, Giulia Gaggi, Barbara Ghinassi, Johannes H Wilbertz, Angela Di Baldassarre
pmc-10713827.description: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease and is characterized by the loss of midbrain dopaminergic neurons. pmc-12592972.title: Coral Skeletal Cores as Windows Into Past Symbiodiniaceae Community Dynamics
pmc-12592972.creator: Jose F. Grillo, Vanessa Tirpitz, Jessica Reichert, Marine Canesi, Stéphanie Reynaud, Eric Douville, Maren Ziegler
pmc-12592972.description: The symbiosis between the dinoflagellate Symbiodiniaceae family and reef‐building corals underpins the productivity of coral reefs. This relationship facilitates the deposition of calcium‐carbonate skeletons that build the reef structure thanks to the energy derived from photosynthesis. The loss of Symbiodiniaceae from coral tissues—resulting in coral bleaching—impedes coral growth and can lead to mass mortality if the symbiosis fails to recover.
